content.text: The treaty decreased the size of the German military.

explanationText.text: Germany had to reduce the number of people in its army and limit the size of its navy. Germany was not allowed to have submarines or an air force.

content.text: The treaty forced Germany to give up a significant amount of territory.

explanationText.text: Germany had to give land to Belgium, Czechoslovakia, Poland, France, and the League of Nations, among others.

content.text: The treaty made Germany accept responsibility for the war.

explanationText.text: In a part of the treaty known as the War Guilt Clause, Germany had to agree that it started World War I.

content.text: The treaty required Germany to make payments to the Allied governments.

explanationText.text: Germany had to pay back Allied governments for their wartime losses. The exact amount that Germany was expected to pay was determined after the treaty was signed.
